extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/agents handling after-final practice, transitional after-final submissions, and requests for continued examination (RCEs)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules from the MPEP for handling replies after final Office actions, transitional after-final submissions under 37 CFR 1.129, and Requests for Continued Examination under 37 CFR 1.114, including eligibility, timing, content, processing, and form-paragraph usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s amendment may not be made more than 6 months from the date of the final Office action, because the application would be abandoned by operation of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not authorize or rely on examiner’s amendments beyond 6 months after mailing of the final Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant authorization to make amendment (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has not been filed within 2 months of the final Office action, applicant’s authorization to make an amendment to place the application in condition for allowance must be made either within the 3-month shortened statutory period or within an extended period obtained by petition under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a complete first reply is not filed within 2 months, ensure authorization is given within the 3-month SSP or obtain extension by petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendment correcting formal matters (no extension fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s amendment correcting only formal matters identified for the first time after a reply to a final Office action does not require an extension fee because the reply put the application in condition for allowance except for correction of formal matters not previously required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only formal corrections newly required by the examiner remain, entry by examiner’s amendment may occur without paying extension fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) — petition and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requires a petition and the appropriate fee provided in 37 CFR 1.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions needed to place an application in condition for allowance (e.g., when examiner’s amendment needed after SSP) must be obtained via petition/fee; authorization to make the petition of record may be given to the examiner with specified deposit-account charging instructions but oral telephonic credit-card instructions to Office employees are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of authorization to charge deposit account
rubrics_metrics.description: When authorization is given to the examiner to make a petition for extension and charge a deposit account, the authorization must be made of record in an examiner’s amendment indicating the name of the person making the authorization, when it was given, the deposit account number, the length of the extension requested, and the amount to be charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 13.02.02 for telephone authorizations; ensure all required details are recorded in the examiner's amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing priority for replies after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies after final should be processed and considered promptly by all Office personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely handling by support staff and examiners is required; do not unduly delay processing of after-final replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies after final considered only if timely or petitioned
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies after final should not be considered by the examiner unless they are filed within the shortened statutory period (SSP) or are accompanied by a petition for an extension of time and the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.17 and 1.136(a)); this applies to supplemental replies filed after the first reply as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure replies are within the SSP or accompanied by proper petition/fees, otherwise the examiner will not consider them (see MPEP § 710.02(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after SSP (no extension fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews may be conducted after expiration of the shortened statutory period for reply to a final Office action but within the 6-month statutory period for reply without payment of an extension fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews are permitted up to 6 months after final without extension fees; do not confuse interview allowance with filing of substantive replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal matters identified after reply may prompt Ex parte Quayle
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal matters identified for the first time after a reply to a final Office action, which require action by applicant to correct, may be required in an Ex parte Quayle action if the application is otherwise in condition for allowance. No extension fees would be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only formal corrections remain, treat via Ex parte Quayle practice; avoid charging extension fees in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawing finality to reopen prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is to be reopened after a final Office action has been replied to, the finality of the previous Office action should be withdrawn to avoid abandonment and the payment of extension fees (e.g., where a new reference renders a claim unpatentable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office action should begin with a statement withdrawing finality and may use Form Paragraph 7.42; see MPEP § 706.07(d) for procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.129 transitional after-final eligibility (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.129(a), applicants in applications (other than reissue or design) pending at least two years as of June 8, 1995 are entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits after final rejection if the submission and the fee set forth in § 1.17(r) are filed prior to filing an appeal brief and prior to abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission timely filed and fee paid automatically withdraw finality; available only for qualifying pre- and as-of-date applications (filed on or before specified dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.129 — scope of permissible submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'submission' under 37 CFR 1.129(a) includes, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement, an amendment to the written description, claims or drawings, and a new substantive argument or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions can be IDS, amendments, or new arguments/evidence, but any amendment entered as result of payment of the fee may not introduce new matter into the disclosure (35 U.S.C. 132).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.129 — limits and non-availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 37 CFR 1.129(a) do not apply to any application filed after June 8, 1995; not available for reissue, design, or reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check filing dates and application type before invoking transitional after-final practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling conflicting proposed amendments under 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant has filed multiple proposed amendments which, when entered, would conflict with one another, specific instructions for entry or non-entry of each such amendment should be provided upon payment of any fee under 37 CFR 1.17(r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should provide clear instructions about which amendments to enter when submitting under 1.129(a); absent instructions, submissions will be entered in filing order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonresponsive submission under 1.129(a) — shortened statutory period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a timely submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) is not fully responsive to the prior Office action, but appears to be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply, applicant is given a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer, to submit a complete reply (this supersedes the prior Office action time period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 7.42.02 to notify applicant; time period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). The examiner must set forth reasons why the submission is not fully responsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: First action after 1.129(a) submission may be final under conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission and payment of the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(r), the next Office action on the merits may be made final only under the conditions for making a first action in a continuing application final set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.42.03 may be used to make an action final following a submission under 1.129(a); set shortened statutory period to three months, with special handling if first reply filed within two months and advisory action delayed, but never extend beyond six months from mailing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.114 RCE applicability (conditions for filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.114 provides for RCE practice applicable to utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or international applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995; RCEs do not apply to provisional applications, applications filed under 111(a) before June 8, 1995, international applications filed under 363 before June 8, 1995, design applications, or patents under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm application type and filing date before filing or accepting an RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an RCE may be filed (timing constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request continued examination by filing a submission and the RCE fee prior to the earliest of: (1) payment of the issue fee (unless a petition under 1.313 is granted), (2) abandonment of the application, or (3) filing of a notice of appeal to the Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit or commencement of a civil action (unless terminated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on RCE to reopen prosecution after these events unless the conditions (e.g., petition to withdraw from issue) are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'submission' for RCE (content requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'submission' for RCE purposes includes, but is not limited to, an IDS, an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability. If a reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, the submission must meet reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal briefs or reply briefs will not be considered submissions under 1.114(d), although arguments from those briefs may be incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE effect on finality and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant timely files a submission and RCE fee, the Office will withdraw the finality of any Office action and the submission will be entered and considered. An RCE filed after appeal but prior to decision will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal and reopen prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an RCE in lieu of continuing an appeal is possible if done timely and with required submission/fee; appeal briefs and related papers are not submissions under 1.114.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing checklist for RCEs (TC verification items A–H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical support personnel will verify: (A) RCE filed on/after May 29, 2000; (B) application filed on/after June 8, 1995; (C) application is utility or plant (not design); (D) application was pending when RCE filed; (E) prosecution in application is closed; (F) RCE filed before payment of issue fee or petition 1.313 granted; (G) RCE accompanied by proper fees including RCE fee under 37 CFR 1.17(e); and (H) RCE included required submission per 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All these conditions must be checked before treating an RCE as proper; failure of any item leads to improper-RCE handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improper RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more RCE filing conditions are not satisfied, applicant will be notified (typically by Form PTO-2051). An improper RCE will not toll the running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prosecution not closed, amendments/replies will be entered and forwarded for consideration under 37 CFR 1.111; if application is under appeal and missing fee/submission, forward to the examiner for appropriate treatment and notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous transmittal paper resolution (CPA vs RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transmittal paper ambiguously references both a CPA and an RCE and the application is eligible for either (i.e., plant/utility filed on/after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000), the ambiguity will be resolved in favor of treating it as a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other papers filed with the transmittal (e.g., preliminary amendment or IDS) won't be considered in determining whether it's a CPA or RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional RCE treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission is accompanied by a 'conditional' RCE and conditional payment (authorization to charge deposit account if submission not otherwise entered), the Office will treat the conditional RCE and payment as if an RCE and payment of the fee had been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditional authorizations are accepted and treated as full filings for processing purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of proper RCE — entry and ordering of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If conditions for filing an RCE are satisfied, technical support personnel will process the RCE and normally enter any previously filed unentered amendments, amendments filed with the RCE, and amendments filed prior to mailing of the next Office action; absent specific instructions, amendments are entered in the order filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should clarify which conflicting amendments to enter upon filing the RCE; file all amendments by the RCE filing to avoid disapproval of entry under 37 CFR 1.111(b). Consider filing a suspension of action (37 CFR 1.103(c)) with the RCE if additional time is needed to prepare supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for claims and RCEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike a CPA, an applicant does not need to pay a fee for excess claims previously paid prior to the filing of the RCE. However, new claims in excess of the number previously paid for, which are filed with the RCE or thereafter, will require payment of the appropriate fees under 37 CFR 1.16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check claim-count and ensure appropriate fees for new excess claims when filing an RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA treated as RCE (post-May 29, 2000 rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant files a CPA of a utility or plant application filed on/after May 29, 2000 (to which CPA practice no longer applies), the Office will automatically treat the improper CPA as an RCE of the prior application under 37 CFR 1.114. If the CPA lacks elements to be a proper RCE, it is treated as an improper RCE and the time period in the last Office action continues to run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who want an improper CPA not treated as an RCE may petition under 37 CFR 1.53(e) with required items (petition fee, true copy of prior application, entered amendments, unentered amendments to be entered, executed oath/declaration if needed). If an Office action has already been mailed in response to the RCE, file a new application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) within the period for reply.
